existing.description: The University of Lausanne awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard. The scholarship is paid for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme at CHF 1,600 per month, and recipients are exempt from the standard course registration fees, with only the CHF 80 semester fees remaining payable. UNIL states explicitly that the amount does not constitute full funding, since about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne. Applications for the 2027/2028 academic year are open until 1 November 2026.
eligibility: Hold a foreign university degree recognised as equivalent to a Swiss university bachelor's degree (180 ECTS credits) before starting the Master's programme at UNIL
Have achieved outstanding academic results during those studies
Hold a minimum C1 level in French for programmes taught in French, or in English for programmes taught in English
Not be currently enrolled at UNIL
Have paid the non-refundable administrative fee of CHF 200
Not have already begun a Master's programme at UNIL, and not be in the preparatory year
Applicants who already hold a foreign master's degree may apply, but priority is given to applicants holding only a bachelor's degree
existing.eligibility_summary: Exclusively for students who have graduated from a foreign university with a qualification equivalent to a Swiss bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and with outstanding academic results, who are not currently enrolled at UNIL, who hold at least C1 in the language of the chosen programme, and who have paid the CHF 200 administrative fee.
benefits: CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme
Exemption from the standard course registration fees; only the CHF 80 semester fees remain payable
UNIL guarantees holders accommodation with the Student Housing Foundation of Lausanne (rent paid by the student)
Possibility to recognise European health insurance (EU/EFTA) or buy cheaper Swiss student health insurance
coverage: Monthly stipend of CHF 1,600 for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme
Exemption from standard course registration fees
Guaranteed accommodation with the Student Housing Foundation of Lausanne (FMEL), at a rent payable by the student
requirements: One single PDF file, downloaded and uploaded during online registration
Two recommendation letters sent by e-mail from a professional (not private) address, naming the candidate in full, and only accepted if sent after the online registration
Certified true copies by post where the degree comes from a non-Lisbon-ratified state; candidates from ratifying states must not send them
CHF 200 administrative fee paid by bank transfer with proof of payment included in the PDF
Incomplete applications are not taken into account
documents: A single PDF containing all of the required documents, in this order: complete and up-to-date CV with photo
Copy of university diploma(s) if already obtained, plus official transcripts of all examinations, with authenticated translation if not in French, German, English or Italian
Copy of the programme description for the last semester or year of the bachelor's degree if the degree has not yet been obtained
Copy of the official language certificate for the language in which the chosen master's is taught, where required
Copy of the secondary school leaving diploma (High School), with authenticated translation if not in French, German, English or Italian
Copy of proof of payment of the CHF 200 administrative fee
Two letters of recommendation sent directly by their authors from a professional e-mail address to mastergrants@unil.ch
Certified true copies of diplomas and transcripts in a university-sealed envelope, by post, only if the degree was obtained in a state that has not ratified the Lisbon Convention
existing.english_requirement: Minimum C1 English for programmes taught in English. Accepted certificates: TOEFL CBT 250 points, TOEFL IBT 100 points, TOEFL PBT 600 points, Academic IELTS 7 points, Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) Grade B, Cambridge English Proficiency (CPE) Grade C, TOEIC 850 points. The language diploma should not be older than 2 years. No language certificate is required if the candidate's mother tongue is the language of the programme or the bachelor's studies were entirely taught in it.
application_method: Prepare a single PDF with all documents in the prescribed order
Register online and upload the PDF through the application portal
Have two recommendation letters e-mailed directly to mastergrants@unil.ch by their authors from professional addresses, after registering
Where applicable, post certified true copies in a university-sealed envelope to SASME, Bâtiment Unicentre, CH-1015 Lausanne
Pay the CHF 200 administrative fee by bank transfer and add the receipt to the PDF
existing.selection_notes: Around ten excellence scholarships are awarded each year. The SASME checks completeness, the Admissions Office (SII) decides formal eligibility, the faculty decides admission to the chosen master's, and finally the Selection Board for the Master's Scholarship selects the scholarship holders in March, with applicants notified in early April. Decisions may not be appealed.
existing.best_fit: Graduates of a foreign university with outstanding academic results seeking a place in a UNIL master's programme in a faculty other than Medicine, and able to supplement the CHF 1,600 per month with their own resources (about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne).
existing.notes: The scholarship application doubles as the application for admission to the chosen master's programme; a separate application to the Admissions Office is not needed. Around ten awards are made each year. Master programmes in Medicine, Sciences and Practices of Education, most of Law, Physical Education and Sport Didactics, Health Sciences, Sustainable Management & Technology, Human Taphonomy and all MAS programmes are excluded. The page warns the amount does not cover the full cost of living in Switzerland.
existing.duration: The minimum statutory period of the chosen Master's programme
existing.application_period: Online application open now for the academic year 2027/2028; all parts of the file (online registration, recommendation letters, certified copies by post where required) must be completed by 1 November.
existing.deadline_display: The online application for the academic year 2027/2028 is open. The deadline is 1 November 2026.
existing.program_type: University excellence scholarship for international master's admission

existing.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.
eligibility: National of a CERN Member State or Associate Member State
Applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals are currently not considered because the Article II.5 Associate Membership ceiling has been reached
Your university must accept that the research conducted at CERN contributes to your doctoral thesis in one of CERN's fields of work
You have started or are about to start a doctoral programme at a university
Good knowledge of English or French
existing.eligibility_summary: Nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, excluding applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey while the Article II.5 ceiling is reached. The candidate must have started or be about to start a doctoral programme at a university, that university must accept that the CERN research contributes to the doctoral thesis in a CERN field of work, and the applicant must have a good knowledge of English or French.
benefits: CERN comprehensive health insurance, deducted from the allowance
Family supplement to the subsistence allowance where applicable
Travel expenses to Geneva on joining where applicable
30 days paid leave per year plus 2 weeks of annual closure
Access to a multicultural research environment and CERN's open technical infrastructure
coverage: Coverage by CERN's comprehensive health insurance scheme, with the contribution automatically deducted from the allowance
Family supplement to the subsistence allowance, depending on individual circumstances
Travel expenses to Geneva upon joining CERN, depending on individual circumstances
30 days of paid leave per year plus 2 weeks of annual closure
requirements: Complete the online application before the deadline
documents: Curriculum vitae in English or French
Completed online application submitted before the deadline
existing.english_requirement: A good knowledge of English or French is required, and the CV may be submitted in English or French.
application_method: Apply through the CERN careers portal on the advertised vacancy
Submit a CV in English or French with the online application before the deadline
Optionally attach an academic reference letter and transcript
Attend an online interview with the hiring manager if invited
Accept the offer to begin onboarding
existing.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by CERN and shortlisted candidates may be invited to an online interview with the hiring manager or managers to discuss the application, CERN and the position, and to determine whether it is a good fit.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates in physics, applied physics, engineering, computing or related STEM fields who need their thesis research to be conducted at CERN and who hold the nationality of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
existing.notes: This is a paid employment contract, not a grant, so CERN does not pay tuition: the doctoral student remains enrolled at and pays fees to their own university. Funding figures on CERN programmes are periodically revised, so the CHF 3,907 net monthly allowance should be re-checked against the live page. The nationality exclusion list is time-limited and states that it reflects a ceiling under Article II.5 of the Associate Membership Agreement. Vacancies are published per round, so there is no single annual deadline.
existing.duration: 6-month contract renewable up to 3 years, with the possibility of spreading it over a maximum of 4 consecutive years to allow time at the student's university
existing.application_period: Continuous, round-based recruitment. Each published vacancy carries its own application deadline on the CERN careers portal.
existing.deadline_display: Vacancies are published as recruitment rounds on the CERN careers site, with the deadline set on each individual vacancy. As of 2026-10-04 the Doctoral Studentship page lists live rounds under the reference TSC-2027-1/DOCT (Doctoral Student Programme 2027-1, 12 to 36 month contract).
existing.program_type: Paid doctoral employment contract at an international research organisation, run jointly with a university
